title: Songshan and Xinyi Walk: Sun Yat-sen Hall to Taipei 101
excerpt: A self-guided 4km walk across east Taipei, from the gardens of Sun Yat-sen Memorial Hall through Songshan Cultural and Creative Park and the Xinyi malls to the Taipei 101 observatory at sunset.
content:
This route crosses the east side of Taipei from the gardens of Sun Yat-sen Memorial Hall to the foot of Taipei 101. On the way it passes through the old tobacco factory at Songshan Cultural and Creative Park, then heads south into the malls of the Xinyi Shopping District and finishes at the tower itself. It's about 4km on foot, but give it 6 to 8 hours, because the shopping district and the observatory can each swallow a good part of a day.

Weekends are the best days for it, when the cultural park fills with market stalls and Xinyi has buskers out, though a weekday works well too. Set off in the late morning so that you reach the top of Taipei 101 in time for sunset, and you'll come back down to find the shopping district lit up.

The Route

If you're staying on this side of the city, our Taipei 101 hotels guide covers the options near the start and end of this walk.

Step-By-Step

  • 1 Ride the MRT blue line as far as Sun Yat-sen Memorial Hall and come up at exit 3
    • The hall's own directions give exits 3 and 4 as the ones for the grounds
    • Head south through Zhongshan Park and walk past the pond
  • 2 Wander the gardens and plaza around Sun Yat-sen Memorial Hall
    • The building itself is shut. It closed on 26 February 2024 for a top-to-bottom renovation, and there is no changing of the guard and no access to the exhibition rooms while the work goes on
    • The original target was the end of 2026, but in October 2025 the hall's director said the works were running a little late and would finish in the third quarter of 2027, so don't expect it to reopen this year
    • The grounds stay open and free, and the plaza is one of the best spots in the city for a photo of Taipei 101 rising behind the hall's sweeping roof
    • If seeing a guard ceremony matters to you, the Martyrs' Shrine still changes its guard on the hour through the day
  • 3 Walk north, cross Zhongxiao East Road and go into Songshan Cultural and Creative Park beside the pond
    • Taipei's tourism office lists the park as open daily from 08:00 to 22:00, and walking around it costs nothing
    • Look round the main tobacco factory building, which opened in 1937 as Taiwan's first modern cigarette factory and now holds studios, craft shops and the Taiwan Design Museum (closed on Mondays)
    • [optional] See one of the exhibitions in the warehouses – some are free and others are ticketed, so check what's on before you go
    • At weekends there are usually market stalls set up around the park
    • Until 31 December 2026 the Baroque Garden in the middle of the factory hosts The Luminous Garden, a light installation that comes on after dark, which is worth knowing if you're back in the area in the evening
    • Call in at the Eslite Spectrum building on the east side. Its shops open 11:00 to 22:00, and the third-floor bookshop and music store never close. There are places to eat in the basement, including a Marugame udon counter and a tea house, and the eslite café upstairs runs from 10:00 to midnight
  • 4 Leave the park by the pond and head south-east into the Xinyi Shopping District
    • Work your way south and dip into whichever malls take your fancy; our guide to the district compares all of them
    • Most of the cafés and restaurants here are inside the malls, and many of the malls are joined by elevated walkways, so you can stay off the street for much of the way
    • The Xiangti Avenue Plaza in the middle of the district is a regular pitch for street performers, and at weekends there are often stages and events set up there
  • 5 Carry on to Breeze Nan Shan, the mall with the tall glass tower on Songzhi Road just north-east of Taipei 101 (it's covered in our guide to the Xinyi malls)
    • [optional] With children in tow, try ATT 4 FUN, the entertainment mall next door at No. 12 Songshou Road, or the i-Ride Taipei flight simulator on the sixth floor of Breeze Nan Shan; it's currently showing a flight over Taiwan and, until 24 January 2027, a Godzilla film that isn't open to under-sixes
    • Go out onto the third-floor terrace of Breeze Nan Shan, which looks straight across at Taipei 101
  • 6 Cross the second-floor footbridge straight into the Taipei 101 mall
    • The mall is open 11:00 to 21:30 from Sunday to Thursday, with an extra half hour on Fridays, Saturdays and the eves of public holidays
    • Have a look round, including the grand lobby area on the fourth floor
    • For the Taipei 101 observatory, note that the ticket desk is no longer on the fifth floor of the mall. Since 1 July 2026 it has been on the ground floor of the office tower, so head there, or book online beforehand
    • The observatory is open every day from 10:00 to 21:00. An adult ticket for the 88th and 89th floors costs NT$600, the Priority Pass that skips the queue is NT$1,200, and the 101st floor costs NT$380 on top. Children under 115cm go free

Once you're back down from Taipei 101, take another wander round the shopping district, which looks at its best after dark.

Where to Eat

  • Eslite Spectrum basement, at the cultural park, is handy for an early lunch. Last orders at the udon counter are at 21:00
  • Din Tai Fung has a branch on the basement level of the Taipei 101 mall, open roughly 10:45 to 20:30. The queue is long at weekends, so take a ticket on arrival and look round the mall while you wait
  • Breeze Nan Shan has a food hall in the basement, and a row of high-end restaurants with views of Taipei 101 on the 46th to 48th floors
  • Our Xinyi food and drink guide has more ideas, from the mall food courts to the independent places in the side streets

Best Time to Go

Saturday and Sunday are the liveliest days. The cultural park's courtyards fill with markets and events, and Xinyi has more buskers. Weekdays are quieter in both places, which suits you if you'd rather browse than watch.

Avoid Monday if you want to visit the Taiwan Design Museum, which is closed that day. Everything else on the route opens daily.

Plan your start around sunset. Aim to be at the observatory about an hour before the sun goes down, which in late October and November is around 17:10 to 17:25, so that you see the city in daylight, at dusk and lit up on one ticket. Check the sky before you buy, because on a cloudy day there's little to see from the top. In typhoon season, between summer and autumn, check the forecast too, as attractions close when the city declares a typhoon day.

Getting There and Back

Start: exit 3 of the blue line's Sun Yat-sen Memorial Hall stop. Exit 4 also serves the hall, and exit 5 is the one to use if you only want the cultural park.

Finish: Taipei 101/World Trade Center station on the red line. Exit 4 runs underground straight into the basement of the Taipei 101 mall, so you don't need to go outside. Taipei City Hall station on the blue line, at the north end of the shopping district, is the other option.

The walk works in reverse as well. Start at Taipei 101 when the observatory opens at 10:00, shop your way north, and finish in the cultural park, where the Eslite bookshop stays open all night.

Common Questions

How long does the Songshan and Xinyi walk take?

The walking itself is about 4km, which is roughly an hour at an easy pace. With time in the park, the malls and the observatory, plan on six to eight hours.

Is Sun Yat-sen Memorial Hall open?

Only the grounds. The main building has been closed since February 2024, and the latest statement from the hall's director puts the end of the works in the third quarter of 2027. The gardens, the pond and the plaza are open and free.

How much does the Taipei 101 observatory cost?

An adult ticket is NT$600, the Priority Pass is NT$1,200, and visiting the 101st floor adds NT$380. Children under 115cm are free. Concession tickets need a Taiwanese ID and have to be bought in person.

Is any of the walk free?

Most of it. The memorial hall's grounds, Songshan Cultural and Creative Park, the Eslite building and the malls cost nothing to enter. You only pay for ticketed exhibitions, i-Ride and the observatory.

Is it a good walk for a rainy day?

Partly. The first half is outdoors, through two parks. From Xinyi onwards you can stay under cover in the malls and on the covered walkways most of the way to Taipei 101. Our rainy-day guide has more indoor ideas.

Carry On Walking

The Daan walk begins at Jianguo Flower Market, a few stops west along the blue line, and takes in Daan Forest Park and Yongkang Street. From Taipei 101 station the red line runs direct to Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall, the starting point of the Zhongzheng walk past the city's colonial-era buildings.
